{{Short description|American mathematician (1941–2023)}}
[[File:Stephanie Alexander.jpg|alt=The mathematician Stephanie Alexander stands in front of a steel plate sculpture of the Boy Surface.|thumb|Stephanie Alexander at [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach.]]]]
'''Stephanie Brewster Brewer Taylor Alexander''' (September 1, 1941 – November 20, 2023)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crematory |first=Renner-Wikoff Chapel & |title=Obituary for Stephanie Alexander {{!}} Renner-Wikoff Chapel & Crematory |url=https://www.renner-wikoffchapel.com/obituary/Stephanie-Alexander |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=Obituary for Stephanie Alexander {{!}} Renner-Wikoff Chapel & Crematory |language=en}}</ref> was an American [[mathematician]], a [[professor]] of mathematics at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].<ref>[https://math.illinois.edu/directory/faculty-by-type Emeritus faculty], UIUC Mathematics, retrieved 2014-06-16.</ref> Her research concerned [[differential geometry]] and [[metric space]]s.<ref name="mathtimes">{{citation|title=Distinguished Mathematical Research award recipients|journal=Math Times|publisher=UIUC Mathematics Department|date=Fall 2004|page=3|url=http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/mathtimes_fa04.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150419185219/http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/mathtimes_fa04.pdf|archive-date=2015-04-19}}.</ref>

==Biography==
Alexander was born in [[Los Angeles]] and raised in [[Vancouver]], British Columbia, and [[London, Ontario]]. She was a graduate of [[Mount Holyoke College]].<ref name=":0" />

She earned her Ph.D. from UIUC in 1967, under the supervision of [[Richard L. Bishop]], with a thesis entitled ''Reducibility of Euclidean Immersions of Low Codimensions''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=4009|name=Stephanie Brewster Brewer Taylor Alexander}}</ref> After joining the UIUC faculty as a half-time instructor, she became a regular faculty member in 1972.<ref name="mathtimes" /> She retired in 2009<ref name="calendar">{{citation|url=https://math.illinois.edu/system/files/inline-files/math-calendar2012.pdf|title=Mathematics Calendar 2012|page=October|publisher=UIUC Mathematics Department}}</ref> and died in 2023.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Stephanie Alexander Obituary (2023) - Urbana, IL - The News-Gazette |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/news-gazette/name/stephanie-alexander-obituary?id=53738822 |access-date=2023-12-09 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref>

== Mathematical Work ==
Alexander's most significant achievements were in relation to the study of metric spaces with curvature bounds. Of particular importance was her work with Bishop to establish a concept of curvature bounds in the style of Alexandrov geometry for [[Pseudo-Riemannian manifold|semi-Riemannian manifolds]] and [[Lorentzian manifolds]], an early step towards the development of [[synthetic geometry]] in a Lorentzian setting.<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=0804.2493 |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephanie B. |last2=Bishop |first2=Richard L. |title=Lorentz and semi-Riemannian spaces with Alexandrov curvature bounds |date=2008 |class=math.DG }}</ref>

==Books==
*With Vitali Kapovitch and Anton Petrunin, Alexander authored the book ''An Invitation to Alexandrov Geometry: CAT(0) Spaces'' (Springer, 2019).
*S. Alexander, V. Kapovitch, A. Petrunin. Alexandrov geometry—foundations. — AMS, 2024. — (Grad. Stud. Math. 236).

==Recognition==
*At Illinois, Alexander won the Luckman Distinguished Undergraduate Teaching Award and the William Prokasy Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching in 1993.<ref name=calendar/>
*In 2014 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to geometry, for high-quality exposition, and for exceptional teaching of mathematics."<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], retrieved 2014-06-16.</ref>
